findings.title: Embedded-post author link lightness values are transposed
findings.body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the dark-theme conversion should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). Instead it uses primary 70% for light themes and secondary 30% for dark themes. Light-theme links become much paler than before, while dark-theme links become a dark grey on a dark background with poor contrast.

findings.title: Custom-message-length lightness values are transposed
findings.body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), and the corresponding desktop modal rule correctly converts it to primary 70% / secondary 30%. This mobile rule instead uses primary 30% for light themes and secondary 70% for dark themes, reversing the intended muted colour in both themes and making it inconsistent with desktop.

findings.title: Topic-map heading changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
findings.body: The mobile .topic-map h3 originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), so preserving the light theme and adding a dark variant requires primary 20% / secondary 80%, as done for the equivalent desktop rule. This line instead uses 50% for both, making the light-theme heading substantially paler and the dark-theme heading less bright than intended.

findings.title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
findings.body: The .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should retain primary 30% for light themes and use secondary 70% for dark themes. It instead uses 50% for both, lightening the light-theme name, dimming the dark-theme name, and removing the original contrast distinction from the adjacent .title rule which was already 50%.

findings.title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
findings.body: The mobile .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should retain primary 30% for light themes and use secondary 70% for dark themes. It instead uses 50% for both, lightening the light-theme name, dimming the dark-theme name, and removing the original contrast distinction from the adjacent .title rule which was already 50%.

findings.title: Category badge-notification still uses $primary scale-color without a dark variant
findings.body: This .topic-list.categories .badge-notification rule still uses only scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), unlike the analogous badge-notification and muted-text rules converted throughout this PR. On a dark theme $primary is already light, so scaling its lightness by 50% does not produce the intended muted colour from $secondary; the PR's dark-theme fix is incomplete for this element.
